observation.visible_scene: A close-up, largely static view of a burning bed of dark, irregular chunks (charcoal/coal-like pieces) sitting on a wire grate. Bright orange-yellow embers glow beneath and between the chunks, while translucent yellow flames lick upward over and around them. The arrangement of solid chunks stays fixed throughout the excerpt; only the flame and ember light change.
visible_changes: The yellow flames continuously flicker, deform, and rise, with flame tongues curling, splitting, and merging from frame to frame rather than translating as a single body.

The overall flame pattern shifts in intensity and shape: tall bright tongues near the top-center early on give way to broader, more leftward and upward flame masses in later frames, then thin out again.
The glowing ember regions under the chunks pulse in brightness and extent, with some areas brightening (e.g., a hot yellow-white patch on the right side in mid-to-late frames) while others dim.
The dark chunks themselves do not move, fall, or break apart; they remain occluded or revealed differently only as flames pass in front of them.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the fire or added fuel before this segment.
Whether the chunks are charcoal, coal, or another fuel, and what happens to them after the excerpt (burning down, ash formation).
The wider environment beyond the close-up frame.
uncertain_details: The camera appears essentially fixed on the same pile, but minor handheld jitter cannot be fully ruled out; background grate position is consistent.
Exact material identity of the chunks is not determinable from the images alone.
Distinguishing true flame expansion from flicker-induced brightness change is partly ambiguous frame-to-frame.
